questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Vector That Satisfies a Ratio in Terms of Known Vectors
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/c2406e6f3cb76f50bfcc73a348b38d93b7a24da8e4314e0b3523bb4cbf143364.png)

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{OB}=b$, and $T$ divides $\overset{―}{AB}$ in the ratio $AT:TB=1:1.$ Find $\overset{\to }{OT}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OT}=\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{AT}.$

First, from $△OAB,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{AO}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-a+b \\  & =b-a.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $AT:TB=1:1,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{AT}=\frac{1}{2}\overset{\to }{AB}=\frac{1}{2}(b-a).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OT} & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT} \\  & =a+\frac{1}{2}(b-a) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}a+\frac{1}{2}b.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/1649e6c4ef2874cda2a7d7428b54220ef2a1790ba4b197c755165c48add0c31e.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+\mu b$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/7cf17440c27765efb34b6a01c12a76ad4e980fc540307e2218227153661db5dd.png)

In $△OAC$ shown above, we have:

- $OA=2.5|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{OA}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OA}=2.5a.$

Similarly:

- $AC=3|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $b$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=3b.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =2.5a+3b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+\mu b=2.5a+3b.$ 

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

$\,$ $\lambda =2.5$ and $\mu =3$

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+3b$, find $\lambda .$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+3b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $3b.$ So, we first draw the vector $3b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094255/assets/eadc3cc79d5c0f9b58bd8afc6864dca8e5f794cf398921e2ad540b491819562f.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $3b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =3b+a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =1
$$

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OH}=h,$ $\overset{\to }{OI}=i$ and $J$ divides $\overset{―}{HI}$ in the ratio $HJ:JI=5:3.$ Find $\overset{\to }{OJ}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OJ}=\overset{\to }{OH}+\overset{\to }{HJ}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OH}=h,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{HJ}.$

First, from $△OHI,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{HI} & =\overset{\to }{HO}+\overset{\to }{OI} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OH}+\overset{\to }{OI} \\  & =-h+i \\  & =i-h.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $HJ:JI=5:3,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{HJ}=\frac{5}{8}\overset{\to }{HI}=\frac{5}{8}(i-h).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OJ} & =\overset{\to }{OH}+\overset{\to }{HJ} \\  & =h+\frac{5}{8}(i-h) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}h+\frac{5}{8}i.\end{aligned}
$$
